Gods & Monsters #2

Tronul zeilor învinși

Amber V. Nicole, Roxana Brînceanu (Translator)

4.20
132,133 ratings14,433 reviews
Rate this book
Fenomenul global și saga romantasy bestseller continuă! Pe fundalul bătăliilor străvechi și al trădărilor sfâșietoare din Lumea Cealaltă, granițele dintre eroi și răufăcători, dușmani și iubiți, bine și rău încep să se estompeze. Pentru că acolo unde există zei, există și monștri…

Căzută în întuneric…
Rănită într-un mod de neimaginat și sfâșiată de durere, Dianna este hotărâtă să se răzbune pe cei care au trădat-o. Ca legendară ig’morruthen, ea tânjește după sânge și poate lua orice formă. Însă forma ei adevărată este cea mai înspăimântătoare dintre toate. Atunci când îi este smulsă și ultima fărâmă de umanitate, Dianna decide să‑și îmbrățișeze latura monstruoasă și să incendieze toate lumile.

Doar dragostea o mai poate salva...
Samkiel, un zeu nemuritor, a fost odinioară dușmanul declarat al Diannei și al celor ca ea. Acum, acesta refuză să creadă că femeia pe care o iubește a devenit monstrul pe care îl văd ceilalți și e dispus să facă orice îi stă în putere pentru a o salva de ea însăși, chiar dacă asta înseamnă să o piardă pentru totdeauna.

Cu fiecare tărâm aflat în pericol din cauza armatei lui Kaden și cu o mulțime de noi amenințări la orizont, Samkiel nu‑și poate permite să lase garda jos. Doar el o poate trage pe Dianna înapoi de pe marginea damnării. Totuși, setea ei de sânge crește, iar zeul nu mai are timp să o salveze și să se salveze și pe sine.



"Un studiu splendid asupra suferinței, dragostei, relațiilor de familie și prietenie. În plus, conține scene fierbinți, personaje de neuitat, acțiune din belșug și răsturnări de situație de-a dreptul năucitoare.” - Overflowing Shelf

"Universul construit continuă să te captiveze și să te seducă pe măsură ce tot mai multe fire ale intrigii se dezvăluie, pagină cu pagină. Practic, privești cu sufletul la gură cum lumi întregi sunt sfâșiate și făcute scrum de Dianna, care le mistuie fără milă, aprinzând fiecare colțișor din ele în numele răzbunării.” - Dear Dominique

"Tronul zeilor învinși nu este doar o continuare, ci o experiență în sine. O poveste despre răzbunare, iubire și alegerile imposibile care ne definesc. Este o carte despre monștri – atât cei pe care trebuie să îi înfruntăm, cât și cei în care ne transformăm.” - The Art of Reading

"O lectură de neratat pentru iubitorii de romantasy!” - Miles of Comfort

About the author

Amber V. Nicole

28 books11.4k followers
Amber V Nicole is a dark fantasy writer with a touch of horror added into the mix. When she is not writing new and fantastic ways to devastate her readers she is probably playing video games or obsessing over anime. Amber loves morally gray characters with their flaws and all and is always dreaming of far off places with dragons, magic, and swords. She loves a good villain and plans to tell many stories showcasing them in the spotlight.
You can find Amber active the most on her Instagram.

June 4, 2023
I’ve said this before and I’ll say it again. NO book needs to be 800 pages. It never serves the story, and in this case you have 300 wasted pages of repetitive and unnecessary fluff.

I take great issue with books that terribly convey emotional turmoil. I’m 25, I don’t need to be spoon fed a long internal monologue about trauma every 50 pages. We GET IT. Dianna spent 1000 years being subjugated by a man who didn’t care about her and held her sister as collateral to force her to commit horrific acts. Her sister was killed. I understand and appreciate the rampage. BUT SERIOUSLY- after 200 pages we should get on with it. None of her choices made sense. Why didn’t she just team up with Samkiel to try to take down Kaden? Then she could go buck wild and incinerate the entire world if she wanted. And the author continued to tell us over and over that she can’t trust anyone because of Kaden, and she can’t stand to be near Samkiel because she feels responsible for her sister’s death. Then it’s supposed to be some grand reveal near the end that she hesitated and that’s where so much guilt comes from?? WE KNOW. YOU TOLD US 30x. I get it. She’s a monster, no one can love her. Boo hoo. OBVIOUSLY Samkiel does! She even admits it over and over that he does xyz, he must really care about me. So frustrating that the fantastic plot gets lost in the poor and rambling writing.

Of course, the last 100 pages was great plot-wise. Prophecies coming to fruition, powers returning, betrayals, worlds torn asunder. It’s all very titillating, but it SHOULD NEVER TAKE THAT DAMN LONG.

“you’re a fool if you think i would be happy in a world where you did not exist.”


— The Throne of Broken Gods picks up immediately after The Book of Azrael and takes you on the most intense ride. this book revolves around the aspect of grief and overcoming it, seeking revenge on those who betrayed you and working through the phases you go through after a permanent loss of a loved one

➷ the world building expands in this book and the story is told within multiple POVs from the side characters. i felt that was the best addition to this book bc we got to learn more about the hand and their backgrounds - i did not once find the pov switch confusing.

➷ i love The Hand so so much except vincent!! he can fr go drop dead that little traitorous weasel. the found family aspect between them all is so precious and i loved that they never once gave up on dianna bc they all knew she was hurting. they welcomed and accepted her as their own, even after everything she done in the first half of the book. i loved when she finally accepted them bc she desperately needed that family bond, and that’s exactly what they provided her with. my heart broke into little pieces for at the end for cameron, that funny, chaotic, precious man has my whole heart! he deserves his happy ending w xavier :((

“we can do this dance until this world burns and the next takes its place, but i will still choose you.”


➳ dianna is in her villain era in this book and she is hell bent on destruction and revenge to those who wronged her. her character deals with grief in different stages throughout the story — she’s lost and so hurt in this book and you can’t help but feel sympathy for her as everyone she considered to be her friends betrayed her. her story is absolutely heartbreaking and it’s it’s so understandable on why she is so guarded and why it’s difficult for her to trust people around her. the grief she felt was tangible, and i felt myself wanting to reach out and give her the biggest hug while reading bc there were some aspects where my heart ached for her.

➳ samkiel, omg this man can do no wrong!! he gives off “touch her and you die” throughout the entire book. he is so head over heels in love w dianna and he would go through any lengths to protect her and help her but that only ignites dianna’s fury and it constantly leaves samkiel in complete agony watching her fall apart. the way he loves every flaw and jagged piece of her had me SWOONING. he never once gave up on her bc he knows he will get his dianna back, it will only just take time. he was so incredibly loyal to her and did not care how her actions were hurting him, bc deep down she is still that dianna he fell in love with.

the relationship between samkiel and dianna is best described as “raw and messy” - the slow burn was absolutely delicious tho and when it comes to the spice, all that tension and angst fr made up for it. i’m so glad that it wasn’t rushed — it is so sensual and explosive when it finally happens.

“do it.” i angled the tip of her blade above my heart. “if you are truly gone, i refuse to live in a world without you, so you’ll have to angle it farther to the right. that’s where a god’s heart lies, and mine already belongs to you, so do with it what you will.”


— my only complaints with this book are that it's really lengthy. i felt myself zoning out throughout the book bc things constantly felt repetitive especially the excessive overuse of "a lock on a door in a house rattled." it got so irking. also this book was unnecessarily dragged out — especially dianna’s vengeance and constantly blaming herself for what happened to gabby. the author could’ve cut out 200 pages and the point would have still gotten across to the readers. and finally, the plot twists were not really surprising once the big revelations happened bc they were openly hinted throughout the book.

— this book ends on another cliffhanger, so i can't wait to see what happens in the next book even tho it will probably be a long wait!!

Honestly, I would say this one is better than The Book of Azrael. I loved how character driven it was, enjoyed the plot and the twists and turns. Really liked how Dianna's grief was handled. I appreciated that we are given a recap of sorts in the beginning.

"A thousand plus worlds he has seen, yet when he dreams, he dreams of you."

The star of the book is hands down, Dianna. Yes there was a moment when she irritated me a bit but considering her situation and what she was going through, it's something am willing to look past. Dianna is fierce, her powers are perfectly utilised and suits her personality.

Samkiel kind of took the backseat for me in this. Dianna just overpowered his presence in every way possible. But I loved how patient he was with her throughout the book. Believe me, she pushes him unreasonably and my guy handled it maturely. Seriously tho, imagine a guy being patient, understanding and pushing for mature conversation, never making her feel unloved- that's Samkiel. Love him yet? 👀

The side characters provided interesting group dynamics. Kaden was...Kaden 🤦‍♀️ The thing about an amata was predictable, saw it coming miles away but the rest of the plot twists were chef's kiss 🤌

The romance was angsty. The smut was juicy. Dianna and Samkiel's chemistry is HOT 🥵

I liked the ending. There was a moment when I actually gasped and had to reread it cause I could not believe that happened. The cliffhanger is not as bad as the first book, but still makes me anticipate the next book.

~•~•~

Do I remember it? No

Who gave these emotional idiots unlimited power? I’d like to speak to a Manager because this is out of hand. I’m honestly wondering if I read the same book as everyone else at this point because this was nowhere close to a 5 star or even a 4 star read. I had similar issues with this book as I did with the previous book, but the most glaring issue was Dianna.

The author should have written Dianna as 35 instead of 1000+. Her murderous rampage felt so excessive knowing that her sister lived 1000 years. I could get behind calculated revenge, but it’s implied that she fed off numerous innocents to beef up her power. It makes sense that she would grieve, but all the “burn the world down” nonsense was too much. There were literally 400+ pages dedicated to her temper tantrum and as soon as she finished she fell straight into an insecure thought spiral about how no one could ever love her because she was too evil, blah blah blah. Again, she is 1000, this is such immature behavior and I have no time for it.

Another issue was the length of the book. I honestly really hate the audiobook narrator and probably should have read the book the old fashioned way, but I’d likely still be reading it in 2025 if I had tried. It is TOO long and too much time is dedicated to Dianna’s “villain phase” to hold my interest. There were also one or two too many sex scenes and I wasn’t a fan of how they were written. Don’t even get me started on her calling him “Sami” during sex, major cringe. 🤢 Side note… The author really thought she did something with that whole “and a lock on a door in a house rattled” business. I thought it was lame the first time she wrote it and then she decided to write it legitimately like 15 more times. 🙄

I don’t dislike Samkiel, but he kind of felt like a side character in this one. I’m not really feeling their connection the way other people seem to. 🤷🏼‍♀️ There’s a lot of emphasis on him accepting every part of her, but she frankly needed someone to tell her some hard truths and snap her out of it. I personally felt that his approach was too passive which wasn’t attractive to me. None of the reveals surprised me in the slightest but I could see them taking the story in an interesting direction. Perhaps now that Dianna is past her villain era I can finally enjoy the series. 🍿🥤

"When I burn this world to embers, and you paint me as the villain, remember, I really did try to be good ......once."

Dianna has lost her last shreds of humanity and the whole world is going to pay for her pain. Picking up right where we left Dianna and the aftermath of the devastating events that took place in The Book of Azrael, vengeance is consuming Dianna's every breathe and she is ready to destroy the whole world to get it. Only one person stands in her way, the God King. Samkiel, refuses to believe that Dianna has turned into the monster everyone keeps telling him she is, can he reach her before she is forever lost to her bloodlust and thirst for revenge?

"I always thought of myself as a monster, and now I suppose it's true. You have no idea what I have done. All I will do. I used to hate that part of me. I didn't realize how freeing it would be just not to care and fully embrace it."

This book was so emotional and heart wrenching but somehow was also really funny and fun to read! All of the characters are so well written and fleshed out and there were so many new facets to this follow-up book that I thought made it even better than the first book! The world building continues to be well developed and detailed and the new, found family dynamic that this book explores is EVERYTHING!!! The balance between dealing with serious subject matters and also more lighthearted banter and character relationships was expertly done and helped keep the story moving. I thought at times it felt a little overwritten and probably didn't need to be so long but overall, I really, really enjoyed this book so much!

"I am a creature born of chaos, born to destroy you. You are the protector of all twelve realms and every dimension in between. Shall we be what we were always destined to be, lover?"

Dianna-She is my QUEEN! Dianna absolutely delivered in this book. She was unforgiving, terrifying and lethal. Seeing her unleashed in all her glorious brutality was thrilling but also her pain was palpable, and you couldn't help but feel for her. She is always the most entertaining character on the page and I love her quick wit and her banter with Samkiel is unmatched! Her character development in this book is so beautiful and I loved seeing her make new relationships but it's all about her and Samkiel! 😍 One of the best enemies to lovers I have ever read.

Do it, if you are truly gone, I refuse to live in a world without you, so you'll have to angle it farther to the right. That's where a God's heart lies, and mine already belongs to you, so do with it what you will."

Samkiel-This man is PERFECT. His absolute and unwavering devotion and belief in Dianna was so amazing. Even when she gave him zero hope and is literally stabbing him, this man never falters in his love for her or his determination to save her from herself. He is willing to burn the world for her. The chemistry between him and Dianna is white hot!! I can't get enough of them! 🥰

"We swore that no matter what happened, we would try to bring her back because if Samkiel loved her, she was also ours."

The Hand- Aaah! I love this group of Celestials so much!!! The way this book really leaned into the found family theme with this group was one of my absolute favorite things and really made this book stand apart. I loved every aspect of their dynamic. Cameron and Xavier are my new obsession!! How can they be so perfect? Cameron is the best and made me laugh the entire book. And Logan and Nev are couple goals. I loved getting to know Imme more and Vincent......(nevermind!) I am so invested in them all and I am scared for all my babies!!!

Sigh, so yes, it does end on another cliffhanger, so we are sentenced to another long torturous wait until we find out the fates of our beloved characters. 😭 I leave you with more quotes I loved in the meantime. 😍

"If you wanted me on my knees, Dianna, all you had to do is ask. You know that."


Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (I am NOT exaggerating!!!)


Spice Meter: 🌶️🌶️🌶️


❗This review contains some minor spoilers❗


The way my entire psyche is utterly destroyed by this book is not even a joke. I am devastated and a pitiful, horny wreck. Where do I even begin with this masterpiece? The plot? It's magnificent. It is so complex and well-thought-out, full of suspense, and major plot twist after major plot twist. The writing? It was so beautiful that had me melting into a pathetic puddle on the floor. The lore and world-building in general are fascinating and even better developed than in the first book. Many questions both from the previous book and this one are answered, even as new mysteries arise. From beginning to end this book is funny and devastating, sexy and full of action, romance, and betrayal. Also, that ending, even if it isn't as horrific as the one in The Book of Azrael, still left me reeling, shaking, and making feral alien noises in the middle of the night. I don't know how I survived it. I need more. NOW!!!

Moreover, that feeling I got as soon as I started reading this and realised how much I've missed these characters is unfathomable. Dianna in her full-force villain era is transcendent. She is so thoroughly wrecked by her sister's death that she left a wake of destruction all around her, hellbent on revenge and bloodlust. Sexy, right? 😏😏 Her grief affects every action and every decision she makes, uncaring of who she hurts or what she destroys. Then there's how she gradually begins to heal, even if her methods were often questionable, which shows just how remarkable her character arc is. She had some much-needed help, though. Samkiel, the devastatingly handsome World Ender, has set the bar so high there is no conceivable possibility in this reality where someone can reach him. He could teach these 'real' men a thing or two about romance and loyalty. Never once did he give up on Dianna, even when she slaughters people left and right, betrayed him at every turn, and hurt those closest to him one way or another. Seeing him juggling his hurricane of a girlfriend and his duties as the god king, letting both destroy him but refusing to back down does some truly wild thing to me. He is THE MAN!!!

Furthermore, Samkiel and Dianna have one of the most wonderful relationships in modern literature. The way they support each other even at their lowest makes any other relationship seem like worthless garbage. Flowers and chocolates just don't have the same impact on me anymore, and it's all Dianna's and Samkiel's fault. I need someone to chase me through the worlds and nurse my aching soul back together or I'm not even going to bother, I swear. On that note, I would also like to add that the tension between them and the way it eventually comes undone (pun intended 😏😏) is so gentle and loving it melted my cold, dead heart. Not to mention, the maddening passion that comes forth soon after had me biting my lip hard enough to bleed and kicking my little legs in the air in excitement.

In addition, despite my unconditional love for them, Samkiel and Dianna aren't the only ones that have my whole heart in their hands. Camilla may have betrayed Dianna in the first book, but she seems genuine in her need to repent for the role she played in Gabby's death. This book got me to change my mind about her, regardless of the anger I felt towards her. Besides, Samkiel's cadre, The Hand, includes some adorable, hilarious characters that I would gladly die for. In the beginning, more specifically in the first book, I didn't really like Imogen. She seemed to be kind of a bitch, even though her presence was minimal. I honestly thought she would become another obstacle between Samkiel and Dianna, but I'm relieved that I couldn't have been further from the truth. As it turns out, she is quite lovely, and while her love for her king is true, it holds no romantic feelings whatsoever, despite their history. She even becomes close friends with Dianna. Neverra and Logan are essentially the It couple of the group. They are so sweet and wholesome, I can't help but love them and appreciate their soothing presence after some truly horrifying moments. Also, they have the purest form of friendship with Dianna (even in her darkest moments she genuinely wants to help them and vice versa) and their support of her is unrelenting. Nevertheless, there is one pair that has me in a chokehold, and it is Cameron and Xavier. These boys have eons of unresolved feelings to deal with and all the life-threatening problems just keep getting in their way. It's honestly so frustrating! Even so, they are the most hilarious characters in the book, and before the shit hit the fan, they shared some beautiful moments with Dianna. However, there is one particular member of the group that needs to get his life right. Vincent has a massive pile of mistakes to apologise for and I will not forgive him until he does. Otherwise, he can drop dead for all I care.

I think it's cruel to make me wait another year or so for the next book to come out but I wouldn't expect anything less from Miss Amber V Nicole

A Masterful Story of Grief and Survival



"What have you buried so deeply that even I cannot see?"

This book is an achingly beautiful insight into the complexities of grief and guilt, and acknowledges how they often go hand-in-hand. The agony of loss can be felt through the pages and had me in tears more than once. The imagery of locking part of oneself away so deep in order to move forward, rather than face the trauma head on, is a painfully accurate depiction for those (myself included) who have experienced the sudden loss of a loved one.
This book portrays perfectly how guilt, bitterness, regret, and sorrow, in the wake of immense loss, can become a slow poison that seeps into the soul and erodes the psyche. It especially shows how this toxic combination has no simple antidote or ‘quick fix’ except stubborn survival in spite of the anguish, hoping that one day you will learn how to live on and endure it.
Mental health is a very difficult topic to portray well and genuinely, and is oftentimes glossed over even in literature. But here, depression, anxiety, grief, and everything in between were faithfully represented and it was truly wonderful (albeit tearing-inducing) to read.

Certified Baddest. Of. Them. All. FMC


“Devil,” he whispered, and to him, maybe I did look like the demons from his legends.
“Actually, it’s Dianna.”



Facing utter devastation after the tragic events of Book 1, Dianna is on a mission that is paved solely in blood and fury, leaving her morals and empathy in the dust. Desperate to escape the pain and guilt associated with her loss, she transforms her anguish into fuel for her anger and blood-lust, hunting down all those who wronged her, regardless of the collateral damage left in her wake. It was absolutely haunting to see the havoc caused in this book. Honestly, I don’t blame her. After what transpired I think anyone would have lost control too. The betrayals and torments she’s faced throughout her life were the perfect catalyst to her breaking. I won’t say more than this yet, not until after the book is released, but I will say that Dianna is an incredibly complex character and a refreshing take on the idea of what makes someone a ‘villain’.

“It won't be easy, and there will be days you will feel like you don't want to get out of bed, but I want to be there for you. Every day if you will let me."

Through it all, there was one person who would not let her fully succumb to the darkness inside her. Samkiel/Liam is just the standard and more, and even through all her anger and vileness he still fights for her because he knows she’s just wounded and worth it. That’s love.

Whole Damn Package MMC


"You deserve to be worshiped like the goddess you are," he said, pressing another kiss to my brow.
"I'm not a goddess."
"You are mine."

Samkiel was between a rock and a hard place throughout this entire book honestly. With the weight of all the worries of everyone in the realm and worlds on his shoulders, coupled with his desperate attempts to save Dianna, he barely had a single second to breathe. But, you really get to experience so many new sides to him and his role as King, as well as see his own emotionally struggles and I absolutely adored that. I do not think I could love this MMC more than I already do and he is the standard I will hold all men to forever (thanks for setting the bar so high Amber). I am currently asking myself where I can find one 🙈👀

A Relationship That Is Unbreakable


“If he hurt you again, touched you, I'd level the world"
My lips twisted in a smirk. "You're cute when you're homicidal."

The love and torment between Samkiel and Dianna played with my emotions so much leaving me raw one second, then mending me the next. It was push and pull, ultimatums, realisation, and submission in its purest form. It was so beautiful and painful, but that made the everything all the better. And yes, there is spice🙈. And yes, it is better than I could’ve ever hoped for and is so worth the tension and angsttttt 😩🔥

The Prophecy
The cryptic af prophecy had my mind working overtime trying to figure it out. But learning new elements to it was both exciting and terrifying to say the least 🙈. Im still scared for what is to come though, I know that this is just the beginning… 🫠

POVs From Our Fav Side Characters
The other POVs in this were so necessary to get a more rounded idea of what was truly going on. I definitely loved having more insight into side characters that I had previously overlooked, especially members of The Hand. Kaden’s POV made me want to jump into the book and rip him to shreds. I hate him. I will never not hate him. But it was very necessary and did give his perspective, especially on Dianna which was interesting to ruminate on. I am hoping to see some of these same characters represented in POVs in future books, and seeing where their stories lead amongst all the chaos. My fav side character has to be either Logan or Cameron. They are the GOAT friends to Samkiel and their humorous unmatched (especially Cameron).

Final Thoughts


The ending was insane. Imo much more agonising than Book 1 but in a completely different way. One of my major theories came true, but there was plenty that I did not see coming… I am so scared about the events that will take place in Book 3 (Unreleased Title), but I am prepared to sell my soul to get my hands on it 🙈. I fear the unanswered questions I have will haunt me 🥲 (worth it though lmao).



I received an eARC in exchange for an honest review. Thank you so much Rose&Star, Good Girls PR, and of course Amber Nicole ❤️‍🔥

“I am a creature born of chaos, born to destroy you.” She lifted her blade, pointing it at me. “You are the protector of all twelve realms and every dimension in between. Shall we be what we were always destined to be, lover?”

Their world kept spinning as if mine hadn’t stopped at all.

I have learned from watching so many that grief comes in waves and patterns. It flows, ebbs, and returns, claiming its way through the chest, the heart, and the brain. It seeks what they bury, aching for release from emotions pushed down far too deep.

Why did her name always feel like a benediction when it fell from my lips?

“We can do this dance until this world burns and the next takes its place, but I will still choose you.”

“If you are truly gone, I refuse to live in a world without you, so you’ll have to angle it farther to the right. That’s where a god’s heart lies, and mine already belongs to you, so do with it what you will.”

“A thousand plus worlds he has seen, yet when he dreams, he dreams of you.”

“Love is such a dangerous and powerful emotion. The gods curse it, for it has power. Empires have fallen for it, reduced to sand and scriptures. Worlds have burned for it, and they will once more. Love has the power to touch even the untouchable. Use it.”

My Dianna.

“You’re a fool if you think I would be happy in a world where you did not exist.”

Xavier’s laugh echoed off the walls. It would always be my favorite sound.

Samkiel was just a boy in love with a girl.

Love was nothing but magic in its purest form.

“Mine,” he agreed, and it sounded like a vow. The look on his face took my breath away, and I knew I would never forget it. I would remember it until I was dust between the stars.

My shoulders slumped. I have been stabbed, damn near dismembered, and swallowed whole, but nothing hurt as much as those words. My chest felt like it had caved in on itself. Maybe he was right. I’d waited too long, my own insecurities eating away at me. What if it wasn’t real for us? What if I messed it up like I had so many other things in my life? What if we weren’t even amata, and I just kept him from the one he truly needed? Athos, like every other god and goddess, had said love made you weak and caused you to lose focus. What if they were right?

“I am only ever yours to have.”

“It hurts, doesn’t it?” he asked, nodding toward Xavier. “Seeing the one you love the most completely under the spell of another. It burns your gut, makes your heart race.”

“You are my whole world.”

“How deeply you must love someone that death itself fears taking them?”

“I fear no gods and no kings.”

Plot- 2/5🔆
Spice- 2/5🌶️

After reading the first book I was SO excited to start The Throne of Broken Gods. I was disappointed in the set up of this book. Initially it started out great, with Dianna going on a vengeful rage. That hardly ever happens for our FMC so I was all for it. Get it girl. But then her guilt/shame/pity/trauma spiral just kept going, and going, and going. The plot of the book was at a standstill and everything revolved around Dianna not being able to cope with her trauma.... and stabbing everyone in the process. I love a healing journey but this went on too long, especially when the first book had such a quick plot line. This book felt like it was at a standstill. About 70% into the book, things start picking up again and Dianna and Sami make up, etc. Then the last 30% of the book was jam packed with all the plot. I wish the author would have spent more time focusing on that 30% because it gets really good at the end and I wanted more of that. It almost felt rushed at the end.

Things I liked:
🔘Enemies to lovers
🔘Slow burn
🔘FMC as a villain
🔘Cliffhanger

There is a sprinkling of some nice spicy scenes throughout the book with different character couples. I would have enjoyed them more if I was not in a depressed slump reading about Dianna's self-loathing.

I was surprised this book ended on a cliff hanger because I thought this was just a duology series. I am not sure if I am invested enough to read the third book when it comes out. Only time will tell.

I still definitely recommend The Book of Azrael. It was so good. And if you read this book, just keep in mind the pacing is much different the the Book of Azrael.

••••••••••

If the first half of the book handled grief from Liam’s POV, the second half of the book focused on healing from Dianna’s POV. This girl went through so much in this book and 𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐣𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐲 𝐟𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐠𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐟 𝐭𝐨 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐞𝐩𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐛𝐞𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐟𝐮𝐥, even if there were dangerous consequences of it..

One thing’s for sure, Amber Nicole can handle such heavy topics in a very beautiful wayy… 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐟𝐞𝐞𝐥 𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐞 𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐡𝐢𝐭 𝐝𝐞𝐞𝐩 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐭. "I can barely breathe without you Diana."

Thoughts
I loved the second half of the book, but the first half was a bit slow. The pacing in the first half was inconsistent and the plot dragged at times. The book also could've been shortened and edited, it felt too long. I enjoyed the political intrigue and there were several surprises near the end of the book. The world building was well done, I enjoyed learning more about the history of the Gods and their powers. I enjoyed the variety of types of magic especially the storm magic, and the healing magic. The writing was descriptive, engaging and immersive. I felt so many emotions while reading the book including sadness, heartbreak, happiness and anger. The ending was very exciting and heartbreaking. I'm excited to read the next book!

"There is no place in this world or the next that you could hide from me, akrai." ❤️

Characters
I had mixed feelings about Diana, in the beginning of the book she was very frustrating and rude to many characters especially Samkiel. In the second half of the book she was great, she realized her mistakes and was very brave. Diana's character development was excellent, she found herself again, and let Samkiel help her. I loved Samkiel, he was so sweet, strong, resilient, caring and protective. His yearning for Diana was unmatched, he waited so many years for her. I also loved how sweet he was to Diana and never gave up on her. I was swooning at so many of the sweet things he did for her. The side characters were wonderful too especially Cameron, Xavier, Logan and Nev. They all had their own personalities. The banter between Cameron and Xavier was great! Logan and Nev were so sweet together. I also loved the banter between Samkiel, Diana and the side characters.

Romance
In the beginning the romance between Diana and Samkiel felt one-sided, Diana didn't want to redeem their relationship. By the ending they both explained their feelings for each other and it felt more equal. The chemistry and tension between Diana and Samkiel was amazing in the second half of the book! The development of the relationship was relatable, there were ups and downs just like in a real life relationship. I appreciated that although they weren't great at communicating in the beginning they learned to communicate better in the middle of the book.

3.5 ⭐️ A good addition to the Gods and Monsters series


"When I burn this world to embers, and you paint me as the villain, remember, I really did try to be good ......once."


About:

After the devastating events of The Book of Azrael, Dianna is hellbent on revenge. However, the one person standing in her way is her lover, the God King. Samkiel refuses to believe Dianna is truly a monster and will do everything in his power to save her from herself.⁠ But can he reach Dianna before her thirst for blood and revenge consume her?
⁠
WHAT TO EXPECT:⁠
✨ fantasy romance
✨ gods and monsters
✨ morally grey heroine⁠
✨ cinnamon roll hero⁠
✨ forbidden romance ⁠
✨ forced proximity⁠
✨ 3/5 🌶 (open door/explicit) ⁠
✨ found family⁠
✨ revenge plot
✨ grief/healing journey⁠
✨ betrayal⁠
✨ shocking twists⁠
✨ action-packed⁠
✨ cliffhanger ⁠
✨ multiple POV⁠


My Thoughts:

While I didn't love this story as much as The Book of Azrael, it was still a good addition to the series that dove deep into the characters and expanded on this fascinating world. I truly believe that Amber Nicole is such a fantastic writer with a unique ability to share a captivating tale and evoke strong emotions.


What I liked:


The flashbacks were a great way to give us more insight into Dianna's past. We finally learn exactly what happened to Dianna all those years ago when Kaden changed her, and some shocking revelations. I think including these flashbacks were a brilliant way to expand on an already established character's history and world building without feeling like it's an info dump.


I LOVE the overall story. While most of this book deals with Dianna's grief and healing journey, there's a lot going on in the background concerning Kaden and his plans. Even though we don't really learn much till the end of the book, I love this mystery aspect woven throughout the story because it always keeps me guessing.

The last 20% of the book, specifically, was fantastic. It was an emotional and action packed ending with so many twists and turns I did not expect! And of course, that cliffhanger of an ending (not as bad as book 1), has me so excited for book 3.


The Hand - Xavier, Cameron, Imogen, Logan and Neverra. I adore all of these characters! We were introduced to them in book 1, but it was so wonderful getting to know them more throughout this story and even getting some chapters from their POV.


The spice. Okay, so it takes a while for Samkiel and Dianna to finally do the deed, but it's pretty great once you get there. There's a kiss at 33%, a few sex scenes between side characters throughout, and then finally filthy Samkiel and Dianna smut around 75% and on.


What I didn't liked:


Dianna's actions and reasoning didn't really make sense to me. I understand why she would be upset after the ending in book 1. I even condone her going on a rampage to kill everyone who was involved. However, here's what I didn't understand.

- Dianna killing people not directly involved/innocents.
- Dianna sleeping with everyone and pushes Samkiel away.
- Dianna fighting Samkiel and believing he was her enemy and would stand in her way of revenge, even though he says he is on her side and will destroy all those who hurt her.

All these things, Dianna did to (in a way) prove she's a monster, when all she really did was punish and hurt herself. This was self destructive behavior, and yes, I get that her behavior aligns with the fact she is a monster underneath, BUT I don't know . . . it felt a little too dramatic, even for Dianna.

Dianna wasn't very likable in this book and honestly, it really pissed me off that Samkiel and everyone else ended up justifying Dianna's killing and behavior. The only person who didn't (and I agree with) was Vincent: "You think she is the only person who has ever lost anyone? Cry me a fucking river. People hurt all the time. They don't kill." Fucking preach! What makes Dianna so special that she gets to act like a psycho when something terrible happens? And the fact Dianna suffers no consequences for her actions pissed me off. It felt like I was being lead to believe that because Dianna is the MC, we have to excuse her behavior, but I fucking can't. I may understand why she did those things, but I don't agree with them and could never justify them.

Also, Dianna's transition from being a raging killer who pushes Samkiel away to being in love and not wanting to hurt him was very jarring, and again, doesn't make sense. I guess she was tired of being hateful? This change also only happened when she was powerless so I guess she just gave up being the bad guy? The push and pull between them drove me insane. I felt so bad for Samkiel the entire story. He didn't deserve this.

Side Note: Dianna calling Samkiel, Sami, as a nickname, which came up a lot during sex, was not for me.

Everything about Dianna and her journey EXHAUSTED me, and since this took up almost 60% of the story, I found it easy to put down and I ended up skimming some parts.


The language used by The Hand (who are super old, respected warriors) was sometimes bizarre. They would say things like a teenager in our modern world and it would totally take me out of the story.


Random, unimportant characters would say really insightful things about Dianna's current emotional state, which was very unrealistic considering they don't know her at all. I'm specifically thinking about the guy she almost kills in the warehouse. I think the author did this to reinforce certain notions about Dianna's emotional well-being or perception by others, but having a random character give this insight was strange and unnecessary; especially when Samkiel and others who know Dianna better end up doing this during their POVs.

To the point above, there are A LOT of repetitive monologue type speeches, both internally and externally done by Dianna and Samkiel. There was just CONSTANT insight into their current thoughts and feelings about Dianna being sad...Dianna being a monster...saving Dianna. And while I get these conversations/thoughts should happen to drive home certain points and set up the emotions of the story, it lost its impact after the first few times. Because of this, I ended up skimming whenever this happened.


The pacing was just off for me. Dianna’s revenge plot and healing journey went on and on and on to the point I sort of felt like we were running in circles and after a while I lost interest. And unfortunately, for this 800+ page book, Dianna’s journey takes up about 60% of the story and the last 20% is where most of the plot happens. Because of this, I found myself skimming whenever Dianna had her repetitive revenge thoughts or sad thoughts about Gabby, or when Samkiel skirted around his feelings for Dianna and his pain. I think if this had been 200 pages less of Dianna’s shit this would be perfect.


Overall, the story is good, however, I do think cutting half of Dianna's emotional journey and expanding more on the Kaden plot would have kept me more invested.



Thank you Amber V. Nicole and Rose and Star Publishing for providing an ARC of this book in exchange for an honest review! As always, all opinions are my own.

It’s been a long time, since I’ve experienced a female character that I’ve resonated with, quite like Dianna. Maybe since Arya Stark or Aelin Galanythis? The way she cares with her full heart, protects the ones she loves, and holds nothing back, have to be some of my favorite traits. She might be a little fiery and hot headed at times, but she’s an undeniable bad ass. How Dianna fully embraces being the villain (for damn good reasons), and goes on a vengeful killing spree, brought so much joy to my vicious little heart. I adored the subtle nods to female empowerment, and “if you’re going to be a monster, at least be a damn good one.” 😈

"When I burn this world to embers, and you paint me as the villain, remember, I really did try to be good… once."

After the events in The Book of Azrael, I completely understand Dianna’s anguish, and absolutely unhinged behavior. The amount of grief, emotional damage, and development (for multiple characters), had me sobbing most of the time… yet simultaneously punching the air. Without spoiling anything, revenge is a great part of this book, and I’m HERE for it. The world building and lore expanded beautifully, and I honestly couldn’t get enough of it.

“You could make a river of blood run down these streets, and I would still try because I know you, the real you.” “We can do this dance until this world burns and the next takes its place, but I will still choose you.”

I would’ve read this book for just those reasons, but then there’s my newest fictional husband… Samkiel “The World Ender” aka Liam (or my personal favorite Sami🫦.) He made this book, unforgettable. I’ve never seen such a morally grey or villainess FMC, paired with a classic, protective, hero, that’s just trying to save the world, but would also help burn it down in an instant for her. Maybe it’s the way Dianna helps him through his own immense traumas in the first book? Idk but I will protect this man at all costs! And if you like Cassian from ACOSF… you’re going to love Samkiel in this book, (or at least I did!) I might’ve even thought “Cassian who?!?!” 👀 after getting to know Samkiel.

“Every fragment, every piece of me still left, cares about you. Even the very dangerous and ugly parts.” “There are no ugly parts or pieces of you, and I care about them all, broken or not.”

With so many plot twists, and reveals, (especially in the last 15%) this book left me wanting so much more! This is one of my favorite series I’ve read this year, and considering it will be 6-7 books total, there’s more to look forward to!

“A lock on a door in a house rattled.”

Thank you so much, Cecelia! I had a blast reading this series with you, and please be prepared to read the next one with me 😉(whenever it releases!) You noticed details, and predicted events, that I didn’t even see coming! Not to mention surviving all of the brutal situations with me. This series was heavy, but also a lot of fun, and I’m so grateful we chose it for our buddy read!

“I fear no gods and no kings.”

5/5
Dianna straciła swoje człowieczeństwo. Decydując się urządzić istną wendetę wszystkim, którzy na nią zasłużyli i choćby miałaby zniszczyć przy tym świat, lub sama zginąć, dopnie swego. Z drugiej strony, poluje na nią Samkiel, który chce powstrzymać ją przed ostatecznym zatraceniem się w zemście. Oboje nie wiedzą, że większe zło, budzi się pod ich nosami.

Jak cudownie było wrócić do tej historii! Zakochałam się w pierwszym tomie ale drugi absolutnie upewnił mnie, że ta seria to będzie istna perełka wśród romntasy, choć oprócz samego romansu ma o wiele więcej do zaoferowania.
Dianna jako żądna zemsty złoczyńca, to jest coś na co nie jesteście gotowi. W Księdze Azraela, jest ona tylko kolejnym zbirem wykonującym zlecenie, za to teraz, gdy sama bierze sprawy w swoje ręce mogę wam przysiąc, że będzie jeszcze bardziej krwawo i widowiskowo. Sceny akcji, które wymyśliła autorka, do tego sarkazm bohaterki i fakt, że jest niczym tykająca bomba sprawiły, że zakochałam się w niej bez reszty.
Jednak Dianna i Samkiel to kompletnie inna bajka. Ich energia jest genialna, filtr zabójczy, zabawne przekomarzanie i już nie mogę się doczekać by zobaczyć ich wspólnie na polu bitwy, całkowicie potężnych i niezniszczalnych. Pogromca Światów absolutnie kupi was swoją wytrwałością, bo to jak on o nią walczył, zabiegał i dosłownie czcił...
Oprócz motywu zemsty, pojawia się motyw found family. Mamy szansę poznać bliżej całą Rękę Samkiela. Autorka zaczęła prowadzać nowe wątki między parami, gdzie ja znalazłam już swoich ulubieńców. Przyjaciele mając styczność z Dianną podchodzą do niej z rezerwą lub dozą humoru więc cudownie obserwowało się ich nowe relacje.
Zemsta Dianny to była tylko rozgrzewka bo to druga część książki rozsadza czaszkę. Wiemy, że ekipa Kadena, ma jakiś niecny plan, który zespół stara się odkryć. Na jaw wychodzą nowe tajemnice i spiski, a czytelnikom przedstawiane są nowe planety. Uwielbiam to jak kreacja tej historii rozrasta się wraz z każdym tomem, pokazując że zarówno fabuła jak i budowa świata jest wielowarstwowa.
W końcu to cykl na 7 tomów, 7 tomów, które czuję, okażą się moją nową ulubioną serią.
